events.title: Pysanka Egg Program Group 1
events.description:
During the period of Lent preceding Pascha, or Easter, Ukrainians write pysanky, or decorate eggs, using ancient symbols. From the deep past, these patterns were thought to imbue the egg with magical powers and ward away evil spirits, and they later took on Christian meanings. During this workshop, participants will make their own pysanka using the traditional wax-resist method.  This is a free program for Adults and teens.

Registration is required as space is limited due to supplies. Participants are registering for one class. March 31 or April 7.

Priority will be given to Raritan Public Library card holders that are in good standings. If space is available, non card holders can register one week prior to the event.

This program is presented by the Ukrainian History and Education Center of Somerset, New Jersey.

events.title: VIRTUAL EVENT - Let's Explore : Sargent and Paris
events.description:
Sargent and Paris explores the early career of American painter John Singer Sargent (1856–1925), from his arrival in Paris in 1874 as a precocious 18-year-old art student through the mid-1880s, when his infamous portrait Madame X was a scandalous success at the Paris Salon. Over the course of one extraordinary decade, Sargent achieved recognition by creating boldly ambitious portraits and figure paintings that pushed the boundaries of conventionality.

The iconic Madame X, a beloved highlight of The Met collection, is the culmination of Sargent’s early years in Paris. The exhibition will take an in-depth look at this captivating portrait and the numerous preparatory sketches, and it will be displayed alongside select portraits of Parisiennes by Sargent’s contemporaries. This program is presented by Presented by Mary Vahey.

events.title: Mrs. Bennett Follows the Army
events.description: Raritan's Historic & Cultural Committee presents Patricia Wells in "Mrs. Bennett Follows the Army". Learn about life as a woman who followed Washington's Continental Army during the Revolutionary War. Wives, daughters, mothers, and single women followed their men on long marches and through cold and hungry conditions. Many had children with them. They worked as laundresses, cooks, and nurses. And, yes some were even prostitutes. Spend an hour with Mrs. Bennett and hear about life in camp, on the march, and during battles. Hear what Washington thought of the camp followers! Please register for this event.

events.title: VIRTUAL EVENT - Media Bias in coverage of Israel Hamas War
events.description:
Explore how mainstream media coverage of the Israel-Gaza war has sparked debate over accuracy, context, and framing. Sarit Catz will share her views on how and why mainstream media news outlets are “getting it wrong” in their reporting of the Israel-Gaza war.

Sarit is the Director of the Media Response Team for CAMERA, The Committee for Accuracy in Middle East Reporting and Analysis, where she monitors the media and facilitates letter writing campaigns. During her career in radio and television, Sarit won three Writers Guild of America awards and, more recently, numerous awards for the short films she has written and produced. Sarit graduated with Honors Distinction in International Relations from the University of Pennsylvania while simultaneously earning a degree from the Wharton School in International Business.

events.title: Caspar David Friedrich: The Soul of Nature
events.description:
Caspar David Friedrich was a leading figure of the German Romantic movement, known for his vast, mysterious, and atmospheric landscapes that explored the relationship between humanity and nature. He reimagined landscape painting by emphasizing the spiritual and emotional connections between the individual and the natural world. Mary Vahey will speak about Friedrich and the current exhibit at the Met, "Caspar David Friedrich: The Soul of Nature". It is the first comprehensive one dedicated to the artist in the United States. It features over 75 works by Friedrich, including oil paintings, drawings, and sketches. The exhibition is on view through May 11, 2025.

Celebrate Spring at the Raritan Library with a special tasting of Chinese teas paired with delicious desserts. Throughout the hour-long tasting, learn about the history of tea, its importance in Chinese culture, and the six main categories of tea. Savor three handmade desserts, including tea cakes and cookies, with flavors paired with three Chinese teas brewed in the traditional gongfu style (with time and effort).  Please register for this event!

Presenter Marjorie Wang grew up in NJ, and attended university in Shanghai, where she fell in love with Chinese teas. After an apprenticeship at NYC's Tea Drunk, she began sharing her passion with local communities through tea and dessert pairing events at libraries, community centers, and clubs.

events.title: George Washington Takes Command: The Journey Through Jersey, 1775
events.description:
250 years ago on June 23, 1775, George Washington departed the Continental Congress at Philadelphia to take command of the new Continental Army at Cambridge, Massachusetts. Gen. Washington traversed New Jersey over three days, making his entrance onto the stage of the Revolutionary War. Follow George Washington’s first “Journey Through Jersey” as Commander-in-Chief as he crossed New Jersey to take command of the Continental Army 250 years ago.

This program is sponsored by Raritan's Historic & Cultural Committee. Please register!

events.title: The Other Book Club - The Measure by Nikki Erlick
The Ice Age Show with "Mastodons, Cavemen and Bears - Oh My"
events.description:
Field Paleontologist Mike and Roberta Straka will present the “MASTODONS, CAVEMEN AND BEARS-OH MY” show. This program will highlight the ice age and explore the life of cavemen and the unusual animals that inhabited the planet. We will feature two amazing skulls – a SABRE-TOOTH TIGER and a CAVE BEAR, that our team excavated.  Your patrons will see actual fossils and early tools of humans. Finally, we’ll host the “Are You Smarter Than a Caveman” game show.

In addition, each child will have the opportunity to dig up a real Mastodon bone and help us build a Mastodon! This program is appropriate for grades K-8. Please register!
